original.target_description: Original experiment, group size and cultural complexity; multiple task-maintenance and diversity tests on opening article page; target test unresolved.

notes: Identity independently verified: supplied text is a primary Nature Letter, Experimental evidence for the influence of group size on cultural complexity, by Maxime Derex, Marie-Pauline Beugin, Bernard Godelle and Michel Raymond; printed DOI 10.1038/nature12774 matches the reference. It contains main text, Methods, and Extended Data; its placeholder journal pagination (00 MONTH 2013 / VOL 000) indicates a prepublication layout, so final p. 389 is identified by the opening article page rather than its printed page number. No PDF was supplied. Only n_o is assigned; all other fields and replication are unassigned placeholders. The opening page reports distinct tests of task type (chi-square 3.83), group-size effect on task loss (chi-square 7.62), interaction (chi-square 0.85), and cultural diversity (chi-square 16.3). The neutral description and p. 389 do not specify which is the target. Candidate common group count from Figure 1: 15 + 12 + 12 + 12 = 51 mutually exclusive experimental groups across group-size conditions 2, 4, 8 and 16. For the cultural-diversity model these groups are the response units; the task-maintenance mixed model instead records each task within each group, with group identity a random factor. The 366 male students are contributors/recruitment participants, not automatically the analytic N for a group-level test. No exclusions are specified for the maintenance models in the inspected Methods; performance analyses separately distinguish all-group analyses from task-conserving subsets. Thus 51 is retained only as a candidate for field-scope review, not assigned to the unresolved target; no N inferred from degrees of freedom.
